fields.reasoning: The change set's intent asks for three fixes and offers fix 1 as 'refresh, or refuse with an inbox item'. Refreshing is the better default. It is what the orchestrator did by hand to unstick the runs. autoUpdate already means the owner wants the daemon to follow main without being asked. Refusing alone would still have stalled every run until someone noticed. Refusing with an inbox item stays as the fallback for when a refresh fails, which covers both options in the intent. The refresh runs at every start, not only on re-exec, because a fresh daemon start with a stale guide fails the same way. Status already decides 'current' as version plus plugin (status.go pluginCurrent), so that is the test the refresh uses. Only installed scopes are refreshed, so the daemon never writes into a home or project that has not opted in. For fix 2, the claudecode adapter's hooks show SessionStart and idle but nothing for a rejected slash command. An unknown command is never submitted as a prompt, so the failure has to be caught ahead of time with a preflight check that the skill exists. The UserPromptSubmit grace is a backstop for other agents and other causes. The incident cost 16 attempts on a fault in the machine's setup, so this failure must not use up role attempts. Holding the run with an inbox item matches how other environment failures go to the owner. For fix 3, health already reports per part with ok, warn and bad, and an out-of-date guide is worth a look but does not stop rhiza from running. That makes it warn, as the intent says. A machine-level part fits because guides are installed per machine or user, like the usage hold. The new enum value is an addition and breaks no existing user of --json.
fields.statement: (1) The daemon refreshes guides every time it starts, including after it re-executes a new binary. It does this before it starts any agent step. For each installed guide that status finds (user scope, then project scope) whose version or plugin is not the binary's, it reinstalls that scope's guide for that agent, the same as rhiza guide install --agent <agent>. It never installs a guide where none was installed. A project-scope guide tracked by git in the project's checkout is not rewritten, so the main checkout stays clean; it is handled as a failed refresh. If a refresh fails, the daemon does not start agent steps whose start command names a skill missing from the installed guide. It opens one inbox item naming the failed scope and the command rhiza guide install --agent <agent>, and it starts those steps again once the guide is current. (2) Before it launches a session, the adapter checks that the skill named by the step's start command is installed for the agent. If the skill is missing, the step fails at once with the reason 'start command /<name> unknown to <agent>: skill not installed; run rhiza guide install --agent <agent>'. This is an environment failure, not the role's: it uses up no builder or verifier attempt, and the run is held with an inbox item until the guide is installed and the run is resumed. There is also a backstop. A session that goes idle after SessionStart with no UserPromptSubmit within a short grace fails the same way, with the reason 'start command was never submitted'. (3) rhiza health gets a new machine-level part, guide, listed after usage. It is warn while any installed guide is out of date or missing a skill that a workflow starts, with next: rhiza guide install --agent <agent>. Otherwise it is ok, and it is never bad.

fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/api (go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... -run DaemonGuideRefresh) start the daemon with a fake re-exec over a home and a project holding an older guide (missing skills/rhiza-builder), and show: both installs are rewritten to the running version before the first poll starts any session; a home with no guide gets none; a foreign rhiza folder is left untouched; a current guide is not rewritten; and a project whose older guide is committed to its git repo is not rewritten, git status --porcelain in its checkout stays empty, and the scope is reported as a failed refresh naming rhiza guide install --agent claude --project.
fields.statement: Each time the daemon starts, after a re-exec into a new binary as well as after a restart, and before it starts any agent step, it reinstalls every guide that status finds installed (user scope, then each project's scope) and not current for the running binary (version or plugin files differ), the same as rhiza guide install --agent <agent> for that scope; it never installs where no guide was installed and never overwrites a folder guide install did not write, and it logs each scope it refreshed. A project-scope guide with any file tracked by git in that project's checkout (git ls-files .claude/skills/rhiza is not empty, as a rhiza guide install --project committed to the repo is) is never rewritten: the daemon leaves the checkout untouched and treats that scope as a failed refresh (daemon-holds-steps-on-stale-guide), whose inbox item says to run rhiza guide install --agent <agent> --project and commit the result through a change set, so the main checkout stays clean for close-out's pull.

fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/api (go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... -run DaemonGuideHold) make the refresh fail (an unwritable skills folder) and show: an accepted change set's build step is not started, exactly one inbox item names the scope and rhiza guide install --agent claude across several polls, and after the guide is installed the next poll starts the step and the item is gone.
fields.statement: When the daemon's guide refresh fails for a scope, or it skips a project scope because the guide there is tracked by git, the daemon starts no agent step whose start command names a skill missing from that installed guide, opens one inbox item naming the scope, the error (or that the guide is committed in the repo and must be refreshed and committed through a change set) and the command rhiza guide install --agent <agent> (with --project for a project scope), and starts those steps on a later poll once the guide is current, clearing the item.
